provenance.origin: AI-assisted synthetic drafting and revision based on user review

labeling_rubric.scope: Judge what the resume text supports, not personal ability or real-world credential authenticity.
labeling_rubric.met: Direct or strongly equivalent evidence supports every essential part of the requirement.
labeling_rubric.partially_met: Related documented evidence exists but does not fully meet one or more aspects, including numeric/degree/production thresholds; retain unmet-threshold annotations.
labeling_rubric.not_met: No relevant evidence is demonstrated in the resume, or available evidence explicitly rules out the necessary capability without a qualifying related match.
labeling_rubric.unknown: Cannot decide reliably from the resume; for a language requirement, absence of any language information is unknown, while an explicit exhaustive language list omitting that language may be labeled not_met in this benchmark.
labeling_rubric.hard_flag: is_hard_requirement=true only for independently explicit mandatory/must/non-negotiable wording tied to that exact qualification; placement under Required alone does not imply hard.
labeling_rubric.evidence: Any acceptable evidence span may count; evidence must occur verbatim, ignoring only whitespace normalization. A listed skill can support familiarity but not production experience without demonstration.
labeling_rubric.scoring: Required weight 3, preferred weight 1; met=1, partially_met=0.5, not_met=0, unknown=0 (provisional); calculate from labels, do not embed fixed expected score.
labeling_rubric.hard_gap_interpretation: Currently application reports hard_gaps for hard and not_met only. Separately track unmet_hard_threshold for partially_met hard requirements; do not equate an empty hard_gaps list with passing a mandatory threshold.

alignment_policy.primary: Match by distinct requirement meaning and category plus alignment_terms; never assume model-generated REQ IDs equal gold IDs.
alignment_policy.splits: If one gold compound requirement is split into multiple model requirements, group all split components for that gold label; aggregate status by weakest fulfillment met > partially_met > not_met; unknown if resolution is genuinely indeterminate.
alignment_policy.merges: If a model combines distinct gold requirements, flag ambiguous alignment and do not count it as correct by default; require separate judgments or explicit human review.
alignment_policy.non_determinism: alignment_terms are aids, not a guarantee of deterministic semantic matching; manual review is required for unresolved mappings.
